code:
$ docker network ls
NETWORK ID     NAME      DRIVER    SCOPE
8f3a2b1c9d4e   bridge    bridge    local
a1b2c3d4e5f6   host      host      local
1a2b3c4d5e6f   none      null      local
caption: Every container lands on bridge unless told otherwise -- which is exactly where catalog and catalog-db have been this whole time.

eyebrow: Who's on the network, and what IP did they get
caption: docker network inspect shows the subnet and every attached container's own IP in it.

steps.label: bridge
steps.sub: the default -- an isolated internal network with its own IP range

steps.label: host
steps.sub: shares the host's own network stack directly, no isolation

steps.label: none
steps.sub: no networking at all, for containers that need to be cut off

eyebrow: Reachable by IP -- but not by name
code:
$ docker exec catalog ping -c 1 172.17.0.2
64 bytes from 172.17.0.2: icmp_seq=0 ttl=64 time=0.089 ms

$ docker exec catalog ping -c 1 catalog-db
ping: bad address 'catalog-db'
caption: The default bridge routes traffic by IP just fine -- it just can't resolve a container name. Recreate catalog-db and its IP changes.

subtitle: Hardcoding IPs that change on every restart isn't a real fix -- next, the network that resolves names instead.
